new_statements.quote: [p. 285, table: 'a 1 | CV̀, CV̀C | CV̀V̀, CV̀CV̀, CV̀CV̀CV̀ | 'bozom'] Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345] Remarque. On pourrait poser que la langue ancestrale ne connaissait que des syllabes ouvertes et un accent ... L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.
new_statements.translation: [p. 285] Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them at present shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity [stress] or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again diachronically, when the sound correspondences are interpreted (p. 345). [p. 345] Remark. One could posit that the ancestral language had only open syllables and an accent ... The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not impose this solution for Proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis can be entertained for an earlier stage.
new_statements.citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale (SELAF 357; Langues et cultures africaines 20). Paris/Louvain: Peeters.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (Google Books publisher preview image of Moñino 1995 Le proto-gbaya, printed p. 285, running head 'RÉCAPITULATION CONTRASTIVE') and read it visually. The table of sub-areas of aire a) lists row 'a 1 | CV̀, CV̀C | CV̀V̀, CV̀CV̀, CV̀CV̀CV̀ | 'bozom', and directly beneath it Remarque 2 reads exactly as quoted: 'A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interpr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gbaya 'bozom, like all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka varieties Moñino surveyed first-hand, is a tone language (two level tones in the western area, 'bozom drifting toward a third level per pp. 152-157) with no accent: the author explicitly denies any present-day phenomenon of accent, intensity (stress) or length, and treats accent only as a speculative pre-Proto-Gbaya reconstruction.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None (no stress of any kind per source).
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only qualification is diachronic: an accent is entertained as a hypothesis for a pre-Proto-Gbaya stage to explain CVCV vs CVC reflexes, explicitly not for the modern languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket synchronic statement in the contrastive summary of tonal morphophonology (the 'modificateur relationnel'), covering every language in the study; 'bozom is named in the table row (area a1) that the remark comments on, and Moñino's 'bozom data are his own (900-item list, 200 sentences, a recorded tale; informants from Gbadare 2, 1970-73, pp. 51-52). Word/lexical prosody is meant (accent vs. lexical/grammatical tone); the dedicated 'bozom chapter (pp. 142-158) could not be opened to check for a chapter-internal restatement.
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's 'gbaya 'bozom' = the Gbaya spoken around Bozoum (clans calling themselves bòkòtò, mbaï, all 'bozôm', p. 142 snippet), i.e. Glottolog Gbaya-Bozoum gbay1286 [gbq], dialect Bozom [bozo1251]; Glottolog's own lgcode mapping for this reference reads 'Gbaya Bozom = Gbaya-Bozoum [gbq]'. His data come from the village Gbadare 2. The quoted sentence is a blanket statement over all 21 varieties in the study (it is not inside the 'bozom chapter), but 'bozom is explicitly one of the languages in the table the remark comments on. The closest sister variety, Gbeya/Gbaya-Bossangoa (gbay1287, gbp), is already in the catalog as NO-WORD-STRESS from Ruckstuhl 1998/2007 and Samarin 1966, consistent with this finding; do not merge the two keys.

sources.note: Preface explicitly declines to mark prosody: 'Quant à l'accent tonique, ou plutôt l'intonation... il est impossible de donner ces indications au moyen de signes alphabétiques.' No statement on Baya stress; the Baya part is a wordlist (Glottolog: wordlist). Full book not located openly (Gallica 403 from our machine; not on archive.org/HathiTrust).
